section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Harappan (Indus Valley) site famous for its well-preserved dockyard, indicating a flourishing maritime and trading centre, is:
explanation: Lothal (in present-day Gujarat) is renowned for its ancient dockyard, evidence of the Harappans' maritime trade — Mohenjo-daro is known instead for the Great Bath/granary, Kalibangan for ploughed-field evidence, and Dholavira for its water-conservation system.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' of the Gupta dynasty is associated with the flourishing of the 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems), a group of scholars including the famous playwright:
explanation: Kalidasa, author of 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' and other classics, is traditionally counted among the Navaratnas of Chandragupta II's court. Banabhatta served Harsha; Kautilya served the Mauryas; Khusrau served the Delhi Sultanate.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Vijayanagara Empire's efficient administrative system included the 'Ayagar' system at the village level, which involved:

options.option_text: Hereditary village officials performing specific administrative/service functions
Direct rule by the emperor with no local officials at all
A purely elected village council with no hereditary roles
Complete absence of any village-level administration

explanation: The Ayagar system assigned hereditary village posts (accountant, watchman, etc.) with service-linked land grants — a structured local administrative mechanism under Vijayanagara rule.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: Akbar's tomb, an important example of early Mughal architecture, is located at:
explanation: Akbar's tomb is located at Sikandra, near Agra, built by his son Jahangir. Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's short-lived capital, is a separate site nearby.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The 1905 Partition of Bengal, which triggered the Swadeshi Movement, was annulled by the British government in the year:
explanation: Facing sustained protest, the British annulled the Partition of Bengal in 1911, reuniting the province — a rare instance of colonial policy reversal due to mass agitation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Simon Commission (1928), which faced widespread protests with the slogan 'Simon Go Back', was opposed mainly because:

options.option_text: It had no Indian members despite being set up to review Indian constitutional reforms
It proposed complete independence too suddenly
It was chaired by an Indian nationalist leader
It recommended abolishing all provincial legislatures

explanation: The all-British composition of the Simon Commission, reviewing India's own constitutional future with zero Indian representation, was seen as a deep insult, sparking nationwide protests.
